title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Directors; Key Management Personnel (including the CEO, CFO and Company Secretary) and their direct reports; any other person with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the Company's activities; and any other person the Board designates in writing. Subject to Black-out Periods, ad-hoc restrictions, prior written approval to Deal, post-trade notification, and the derivatives/protection-arrangement/margin loan/speculative-trading prohibitions in clause 7.

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: A Designated Person distinguished only for approval: the Chair must obtain prior approval of the Board (rather than the Chair's own approval) before Dealing.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Spouse (including de facto) or children under 18, a person financially dependent on or acting in concert with a Designated Person, and a trust or company controlled by or in which a Designated Person or close family members have an interest. Deemed to be Designated Persons themselves and so subject to the full Policy.

tiers.name: employees, consultants or contractors (other than a Designated Person)
tiers.description: May Deal at any time provided they do not possess Inside Information. Not subject to Black-out Periods, ad-hoc restrictions, prior approval, derivatives, protection-arrangement, margin loan or speculative-trading prohibitions, which are confined to Designated Persons.

definitions.hedging_definition: operate to limit the economic risk of any Designated Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including Company Securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that Designated Person's behalf

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Company's quarterly results
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after release of the Company's quarterly results

windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after release of the Company's half-year results

windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after release of the Company's full-year results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Chair, in consultation with the Company Secretary, may determine any other period to be a Black-out Period from time to time. Separately, the Company may impose, without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion, additional restrictions on Dealing by any or all Designated Persons, even outside a Black-out Period; any restriction communicated under this clause must be kept strictly confidential.

rules.detail: Derivatives are defined to include s761D instruments 'such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars' and any transaction limiting economic risk, with no venue limitation, so an OTC collar is expressly a Derivative and is banned outright over unvested equity instruments including performance rights.
rules.evidence: The Company prohibits the use of Derivatives in relation to unvested equity instruments, including performance share rights, and vested Company Securities that are subject to disposal restrictions (such as a 'Holding Lock').

rules.detail: Same outright ban extends to vested Company Securities still subject to a disposal restriction such as an ASX-style Holding Lock.
rules.evidence: The Company prohibits the use of Derivatives in relation to ... vested Company Securities that are subject to disposal restrictions (such as a 'Holding Lock').

rules.detail: Derivatives over vested, disposal-restriction-free positions may be used subject to law and the Policy's other provisions, i.e. outside Black-out/ad-hoc periods, not while possessing Inside Information, and with the clause 6 prior written approval that applies to any Dealing.
rules.evidence: Derivatives may be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions subject to compliance with the law and the other provisions of this Policy.

rules.detail: All 'protection arrangements' (defined to include hedging arrangements that limit economic risk, short selling beyond one's holding, and arrangements enabling profit from a price fall) are banned at any time over unvested Company Securities.
rules.evidence: The entering into of all types of 'protection arrangements' for any Company Securities: (a) is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Same outright protection-arrangement ban extends to vested Company Securities still subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Protection arrangements over vested, holding-lock-free Company Securities are permitted only with clause 6 prior written approval from the Chair or Board.

Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar structure is a Dealing (agreement to dispose of securities) and a Derivative (forward contract), and falls within 'protection arrangements' as a transaction that could enable profit from a price decrease or otherwise limit economic risk, so it needs clause 6 approval and is banned outright over unvested or holding-locked shares.
rules.evidence: otherwise enable a Designated Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities.

rules.detail: A monetisation structure over unvested or holding-locked shares is caught by the outright Derivatives and protection-arrangement bans.
rules.evidence: The Company prohibits the use of Derivatives in relation to unvested equity instruments, including performance share rights, and vested Company Securities that are subject to disposal restrictions.

rules.detail: Short selling of Company Securities beyond the Designated Person's holding is expressly listed as a form of protection arrangement, so it is banned outright over unvested/holding-locked shares (7.4(a)) and otherwise requires clause 6 approval.
rules.evidence: entering into protection arrangements includes entering into transactions which: (c) amount to 'short selling' of Company Securities beyond the Designated Person's securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere and is not listed within the Dealing, Derivatives or protection arrangement definitions.

CFDs are named expressly and banned only to the extent short-term or speculative; a non-speculative CFD is instead a Derivative/protection arrangement subject to the clause 6 approval regime and the vesting-state bans above.
rules.evidence: This prohibition includes short term direct dealing in Company Securities as well as transactions in the derivative markets, involving exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative.

rules.detail: Outright ban on entering a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire Company Securities, and on using Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement, with no clearance route and no vesting-state carve-out.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may not: (a) enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities; or (b) use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.

rules.detail: Using Company Securities as security is banned only insofar as it secures a 'Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement' (defined as borrowing to invest in securities using existing investments as security); an encumbrance unconnected to any borrowing (e.g. a court-ordered charge) is not addressed.
rules.evidence: use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.

rules.detail: Margin Loan is defined broadly as 'any lending or similar arrangement allowing a person to borrow money to invest in securities using existing investments as security'; the 'or similar funding arrangement' wording in 7.5(b) is not limited to margin-lender products and, on its natural reading, extends to a bank loan secured on the Designated Person's Company Securities.
rules.evidence: Margin Loan ... means any lending or similar arrangement allowing a person to borrow money to invest in securities using existing investments as security.

rules.detail: General ban on short-term or speculative trading, undefined by a fixed holding period.
rules.evidence: Under no circumstances should Designated Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in Company Securities.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within five business days of the Dealing
clearance.evidence: Any Designated Person (other than the Chair) wishing to Deal in Company Securities must obtain the prior written approval of the Chair or the Board before doing so.

can be withdrawn (if clearance has been given) if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances ... may be made in the Approval Officer's absolute discretion, without giving any reasons ... must be kept strictly confidential.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within five business days of the Dealing
clearance.evidence: If the Chair wishes to Deal in Company Securities, the Chair must obtain the prior approval of the Board before doing so.

clearance.tier: employees, consultants or contractors (other than a Designated Person)
clearance.evidence: An employee, consultant or contractor (who is not a Designated Person) may, at any time, Deal in Company Securities if he or she does not have information that he or she knows, or ought reasonably to know, is Inside Information.

short_term.evidence: Under no circumstances should Designated Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in Company Securities.

exceptions.evidence: the Designated Person is in severe financial hardship and a pressing financial commitment cannot be satisfied otherwise than by disposing of Company Securities.

the Designated Person is required by a court order, or there are court enforceability undertakings, to transfer or dispose of Company Securities or there is some other overriding legal regulatory requirement for them to do so.

invest in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in Company Securities) where the assets of the fund or scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party.
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer.

exceptions.approver: Board (approves timing and structure of the offer)
exceptions.evidence: participate in an offer or invitation made to all or most security holders, including a rights issue, equal access buy-back, security purchase plan or dividend or distribution reinvestment plan, where the timing and structure of the offer or invitation has been approved by the Board.

exercise (but not Deal with the Company Securities following exercise) an option or right under an employee incentive scheme where the final date for the exercise of the option or right falls during a Black-out Period ... and the Designated Person could not reasonably have been expected to exercise it at a time when free to do so.
acquire Company Securities under a bonus issue made to all holders of securities of the same class.
acquire Company Securities under a dividend reinvestment, or top-up plan that is available to all holders of securities of the same class.
acquire, or agree to acquire, Company Securities through the exercise of Company Securities issued under an employee incentive scheme.
withdraw ordinary shares in the Company held on behalf of the Designated Person in an employee incentive scheme where the withdrawal is permitted by the rules of that plan.

where the Designated Person is a trustee, trade in Company Securities by that trust, provided the Designated Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Black-out Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Designated Person.

exemption_authority: Disposal Consent (clause 5.2) is limited to disposals/transfers, not acquisitions, and only for severe financial hardship or a court order/legal requirement, granted at the Chair's absolute discretion. No exemption authority extends to acquiring securities, to derivatives, protection arrangements or margin loans, and clause 2.1 confirms no exemption overrides the underlying insider trading prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy's own Derivatives definition expressly names 'collars', so a purchased put/written call structure is unambiguously caught and follows the 7.2 vesting-state rules (banned unvested/locked, clearance-only once vested and unrestricted).

bespoke_clauses.clause: Margin Loan ... means any lending or similar arrangement allowing a person to borrow money to invest in securities using existing investments as security.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar (borrowing against the collared shares) plausibly falls within 'similar funding arrangement' under 7.5(b) even though the loan proceeds are not being used to buy more securities, creating a real risk the financing leg is banned outright with no approval route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A person who possesses Inside Information is prohibited from trading and this applies even where ... Disposal Consent has been given under this Policy (whether in exceptional circumstances or otherwise).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any collar entry, unwind or settlement remains unlawful if the executive holds inside information, regardless of any clearance already obtained from the Chair.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Buy or sell orders for Company Securities which are placed but not completed outside of a Black-out Period ... the order must be completed within five trading days otherwise it will lapse; and the order cannot be varied.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If a Black-out Period commences while a collar leg is still executing, the unexecuted portion must complete within five trading days or lapse, and cannot be re-struck, constraining execution timing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company may impose, without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion, additional restrictions on Dealing ... even where the proposed Dealing would otherwise take place outside a Black-out Period ... must be kept strictly confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An undisclosed ad-hoc restriction can block collar entry, roll or unwind at any time with no visibility to the bank counterparty.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no stated clearance validity or SLA
bespoke_clauses.clause: clause 6 approval regime contains no stated response timeframe and no stated expiry period for an approval to Deal (contrast the Disposal Consent under 5.2, which is issued for 'a specified time period')
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Absent a defined clearance window, the executive and bank cannot rely on a fixed execution period once approval is granted, adding timing risk to trade date certainty.

summary: A funded collar is very difficult under this policy. The derivatives leg (a purchased put and written call, expressly named as 'collars' in the Derivatives definition) is banned outright over unvested equity and vested but holding-locked shares, and is only permitted over vested, unrestricted shares with prior written approval from the Chair (or the Board for the Chair), outside Black-out Periods and confidential ad-hoc restrictions, and while not in possession of Inside Information. The loan leg is fatal: clause 7.5 bans Designated Persons from using Company Securities as security for a 'Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement', a term broad enough to plausibly capture a bank loan secured on the collared shares, with no clearance route or exemption. There is no forced-sale, price-trigger or financing-disclosure framework because secured financing is meant to be entirely absent. Even a cleared, unfunded collar could not rely on a Disposal Consent to override the insider trading prohibition, and any unexecuted leg caught by a newly declared Black-out Period must complete within five trading days or lapse. Overall, the options legs might be achievable with clearance once shares are vested and unrestricted, but the secured loan cannot be structured as described without breaching the Policy.
